sports.h3: US Open opens without Sinner as Alcaraz returns from injury
sports.summary: The 2026 US Open began on Sunday at Flushing Meadows with world number one Jannik Sinner absent through a knee injury and defending champion Carlos Alcaraz back after four months out.
body: Play started on 30 August and runs to 13 September. Sinner withdrew with a knee problem picked up during his break before the North American swing, ending a run of appearances at every Grand Slam since Wimbledon 2019. Jack Draper also pulled out injured.

Alcaraz opens his title defence against Roman Safiullin after a four month layoff with a wrist problem. He has spoken about the intrusive thoughts that came with the uncertainty over his recovery, and the draw hands him a demanding route with Novak Djokovic in the same half.

On the women's side Aryna Sabalenka begins against Camila Osorio with her top ranking under threat. Coco Gauff arrives in better form after beating Jessica Pegula to win the Cincinnati Open, her first title of 2026.

sports.h3: Tearful Federer inducted into International Tennis Hall of Fame
sports.summary: Roger Federer was inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame in Newport, calling it one of the greatest honours of his life.
body: The 20 time Grand Slam singles champion, who retired in 2022, wiped away tears at the ceremony in Rhode Island in front of tennis greats including Billie Jean King and John McEnroe. Federer is 45 and made his tour debut in 1998 at the age of 16.

His record includes a men's record eight Wimbledon titles, six Australian Opens, five US Opens and one French Open, plus 310 weeks at world number one. Only Rafael Nadal on 22 majors and Novak Djokovic on 24 have won more men's singles Grand Slams.

Federer used his speech to thank his wife Mirka, his idol Stefan Edberg and the ball kids who worked his matches, joking that he had worn more than 5,000 headbands and over 7,000 pairs of socks across his career.

sports.h3: Norrie falls in four sets to Van Assche on US Open day one
sports.summary: Cameron Norrie was beaten 6-7 (6-8) 6-2 6-2 6-3 by France's Luca Van Assche in the first round at Flushing Meadows.
body: Norrie took a tight opening set on a tie break but lost the next three as Van Assche took control. The result removed one of Britain's more experienced men from the draw on the opening day of the tournament.

There was better news elsewhere for British players. Qualifier Toby Samuel came through on his New York main draw debut, while Katie Boulter was taken to a deciding set by American wildcard Carol Young Suh Lee.
Novak Djokovic and Venus Williams were also scheduled on day one, with Djokovic drawn against Mariano Navone in the first round.

sports.h3: Muchova and Mensik take US Open mixed doubles crown
sports.summary: Karolina Muchova and Jakub Mensik saved two match points to beat Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli and win the US Open mixed doubles title and its $1m prize.
body: The all Czech pairing came through a final set tie break thriller to claim the revamped event, which was played in the week before the main draw and drew a field of singles stars.

Bencic and Cobolli had reached the final by knocking out Carlos Alcaraz and Serena Williams in the quarter finals, one of the most watched pairings of the week. Top seeds Novak Djokovic and Aryna Sabalenka went out in the first round to Katerina Siniakova and Henry Patten.
The format again turned the mixed competition into a marquee opening act rather than a sideshow, with $1m going to the winning pair.

sports.h3: Lausanne closes first Grand Slam and lands 2028 Worlds
sports.summary: The inaugural Ecole Mont-Olivet Lausanne Grand Slam ended on Sunday with 513 judoka from 77 nations competing, and the city confirmed as host of the 2028 World Judo Championships.
body: Russia finished top of the medal table ahead of Japan and Germany, with Georgia, France, Uzbekistan, Brazil, Israel, Kazakhstan and Poland all taking gold across the three days at the Vaudoise Arena.

Organisers sold more than 12,500 of the 15,000 available tickets. Swiss Judo president Sergei Aschwanden called the first edition a real success and pointed to strong local and international media interest.
Lausanne will stage the World Judo Championships in 2028, 55 years after it last hosted the event in 1973. The grand slam ran alongside adapted judo and deaf judo competitions in the same arena.

sports.h3: Tasoev and Fontaine headline final day golds in Lausanne
sports.summary: Inal Tasoev won the +100kg title and an all French +78kg final went to Romane Fontaine on the closing day of the Lausanne Grand Slam.
body: Tasoev closed the final block with explosive judo in the heaviest men's category. At -100kg Georgia's Ilia Sulamanidze claimed his sixth grand slam title, beating Simeon Catharina of the Netherlands in the final.
Uzbekistan took -90kg gold through Bozorov in an all Uzbek showdown, while Germany's Anna Monta Olek won -78kg with a tactical display against Yelyzaveta Lytvynenko.

Earlier in the week Yamato Fukuda beat Lee Harim in a Japan against Republic of Korea -60kg final, and Kazakhstan's Abylaikhan Zhubanazar took -81kg gold over Uzbekistan's Arslonbek Tojiev. Attention now turns to the World Championships in Baku.

sports.h3: Gabi Pessanha enters ADCC as three divisions reshuffle
sports.summary: Twelve time IBJJF champion Gabi Pessanha has entered the +65kg division at the ADCC World Championship after returning champion Rafaela Guedes withdrew.
body: ADCC Worlds run on 12 and 13 September, with the bracket reveal show on 11 September and the amateur world championships on the same day. Athletes have dropped out of the -66kg, -88kg and +65kg divisions, with Pessanha's entry the biggest change.
New no gi world rankings landed the same week, putting Andrew Tackett at number one at men's 170lbs, Helena Crevar at women's heavyweight and Elisabeth Clay at women's 145lbs.
UFC BJJ 10 took place in Las Vegas, where Tackett and Brianna Ste-Marie both won their promotional title matches by submission.

sports.h3: Vadnai wins ILCA 7 Worlds in first Hungarian triumph
sports.summary: Jonatan Vadnai sealed the ILCA 7 Men's World Championship in Dun Laoghaire on Sunday, the first time a Hungarian sailor has won the title.
body: Vadnai closed with a fourth and a first in the Final Series races to finish on 47 points. The format sent the top ten sailors into a medal shootout after eleven races of the Elimination Series.

Britain's Elliot Hanson had led going into the final day after the Elimination Series concluded on Saturday, with Greece's Athanasios Kyfidis and Singapore's Ryan Lo among the other leaders through the week.
The championship was sailed in mixed conditions on Dublin Bay, including light nine knot breezes and rain during the middle days.

sports.h3: Platoon Aviation take fourth Royal Cup in Lanzarote
sports.summary: Harm Muller-Spreer's Platoon Aviation won the 52 Super Series Royal Cup at Puerto Calero for the fourth time, with Brazil's Crioula second.
body: The German flagged three time world champions built a seven point lead by day three and never looked back, adding a first and a fourth on the breeziest day of the regatta.

The result was Platoon Aviation's first regatta win since the Royal Cup in 2024. Eduardo and Renato Plass and their Crioula crew from Valeros do Sul Yacht Club in Porto Alegre secured a first podium of this level.
The 52 Super Series circuit heads on with Valencia among the venues lining up major events later in the season.

sports.h3: Scheidt and Sperry crowned Star European champions
sports.summary: Five time Olympic medallist Robert Scheidt and 2008 Olympian Austin Sperry won the Star European Championship at Medemblik after a flawless final day.
body: The Brazilian and American pairing closed out one of the most prestigious titles in international keelboat sailing on the IJsselmeer. They had been chasing after Negri and Lambertenghi struck earlier in the series.
Severe weather across western Europe disrupted the regatta, with only one race completed on day three before storms arrived and further racing was affected.
Medemblik delivered a mix of grey skies and fresh easterly breeze across the week, conditions the Dutch venue is known for.

sports.h3: Norris signs McLaren extension through to 2030
sports.summary: Lando Norris has committed his long term future to McLaren with a multi year contract extension that runs to 2030.
body: The reigning world champion has already started a team record 163 grands prix for McLaren. He said the target of the new deal is more world championships rather than simply seeing out his career in papaya.
The announcement came in the fortnight between the Dutch Grand Prix and Monza, where Formula 1 returns on 4 to 6 September for Ferrari's home race.
Norris won at Zandvoort in the last round for back to back victories, although Kimi Antonelli still leads the drivers' standings and Mercedes hold a clear constructors' advantage.

sports.h3: Red Bull weigh Lawson against recovering Hadjar for Monza
sports.summary: Liam Lawson could keep the second Red Bull seat at the Italian Grand Prix as Isack Hadjar works to prove his fitness after a summer shutdown injury.
body: Hadjar picked up the injury during the shutdown and missed Zandvoort. He says he is healing fast and is targeting a return at Monza, but there are no guarantees either way and he will be given as long as possible to prove his fitness.
Lawson stepped in at Zandvoort and now waits on the team's call. Red Bull have not set a public deadline for the decision.

Elsewhere on the driver market, Alpine confirmed Franco Colapinto alongside Pierre Gasly for 2027, while Yuki Tsunoda's route back to a full time seat looks increasingly narrow despite an impressive showing at Zandvoort.

sports.h3: PSV hammer Utrecht 6-1 as Feyenoord stay winless at home
sports.summary: Champions PSV tore Utrecht apart 6-1 at Stadion Galgenwaard while Feyenoord were held 2-2 by bottom side ADO Den Haag in Eredivisie round four.
body: PSV's win was one sided from early on and pushed Utrecht deeper into trouble at the wrong end of the table. It was the standout scoreline of a goal heavy Sunday programme.
Feyenoord remain without a home league win after four rounds. ADO Den Haag grabbed their first point of the season in Rotterdam, an outcome few had predicted given their start.
Feyenoord also face a squad change, with Eredivisie top scorer Ayase Ueda set to join Lille before the transfer deadline.

sports.h3: Ajax win 4-0 at Telstar as Twente sink Cambuur
sports.summary: Ajax cruised to a 4-0 win at Telstar and FC Twente beat Cambuur 4-1 in Leeuwarden to complete a comfortable weekend for the chasing pack.
body: Ajax had a stress free afternoon in Velsen-Zuid, with the visitors in control throughout against a Telstar side already facing a relegation fight.

At Cambuur, Barcelona target Ruud Nijstad opened the scoring with a strike from distance before Wout Weghorst quickly doubled the lead. Marko Pjaca made it three shortly after half time after a nutmegged assist from Sondre Orjasaeter, and Younes Taha added a fourth.
Cambuur pulled one back in the 88th minute but stay pointless at the foot of the table. Willem II and Heerenveen drew 2-2 in Tilburg, where Devin Haen saved a point in the 83rd minute.

consumer-tech.h3: Apple sets 9 September event for iPhone 18 Pro and foldable
consumer-tech.summary: Apple has sent invitations for a Surprise and shine event on Wednesday 9 September, expected to bring the iPhone 18 Pro and the company's first folding iPhone.
body: The keynote starts at 10am Pacific at Apple Park. It is the company's biggest consumer hardware moment of the year and the first under incoming chief executive John Ternus.

Alongside the iPhone 18 Pro, reporting points to a foldable model positioned above the Pro line, a new Apple Watch Ultra and further smart home hardware. Analysts have counted as many as eight possible product reveals.
Pre-orders may start later than usual this year, with some reports suggesting the gap between announcement and on sale date will stretch beyond the normal pattern.

consumer-tech.h3: Galaxy S26 FE ships with One UI 9 before the flagships
consumer-tech.summary: Samsung launched the Galaxy S26 FE with a 6.7 inch display and One UI 9 based on Android 17, beating the rest of the S26 line to the newest software.
body: The FE model traditionally arrives after the flagships and cuts specification to hit a lower price, so shipping the newest software first is a reversal of the usual order.
One UI 9 is built on Android 17. Putting it on the FE now gives Samsung a live test bed ahead of a wider rollout across the S26 series.
The launch sets up a busy September for Samsung, which is also expected to push its Galaxy Glasses effort on the Android XR platform.

consumer-tech.h3: IFA Berlin lines up AI, robots and smart glasses
consumer-tech.summary: IFA 2026 opens in Berlin next week with AI hardware, humanoid robots, smart glasses and reworked laptops set to dominate the show floor.
body: Preview coverage points to AI running through almost every category rather than sitting in a single product class, from home appliances to notebooks. Robotics has a larger presence than in previous years.
Smart glasses are the other headline theme. The category has grown quickly around camera and audio frames, with display equipped models arriving alongside them.
Smaller vendors are using the show to stake out ground too. Ninkear and GEEKOM are both bringing local AI mini PCs and laptops to Berlin.

consumer-tech.h3: Plaud One rethinks headphones for AI note taking
consumer-tech.summary: Plaud has revealed the One, a set of AI headphones built around recording, transcription and summarising, which will be shown at IFA in Berlin.
body: The device is pitched as a reinvention of headphones for the AI note taking era rather than an audio product with software bolted on. Capture and summarisation sit at the centre of the design.
Plaud has also introduced AI earbuds with built in 4G connectivity, letting them record, transcribe and summarise conversations without a smartphone nearby.
The company has built its business around dedicated recording hardware, and the move into worn audio puts it against far larger earbud makers.

consumer-tech.h3: GMKtec mini PC packs 16 cores and 192GB of DDR5
consumer-tech.summary: GMKtec confirmed the Evo X5 Pro mini PC, built on the 16 core Ryzen AI Max Plus Pro 495 and configurable with up to 192GB of DDR5 memory.
body: The machine is due to be unveiled early next month. The memory ceiling is the headline number and puts the box in range of local AI workloads that normally need a workstation.
Mini PCs have become one of the more interesting corners of the desktop market as AMD's APU line closed much of the gap to discrete graphics for everyday and light creative work.
It arrives into a crowded field, with several rivals bringing local AI focused small form factor machines to IFA in Berlin.

consumer-tech.h3: DLSS 5 leaks early and modders bolt it onto everything
consumer-tech.summary: Code for Nvidia's unreleased DLSS 5 appeared in an early access build of NBA 2K27, and modders have since forced it into Control, Skyrim, Cyberpunk 2077 and GTA V.
body: Members of the RenoDX modding channel extracted the DLSS Neural Rendering file and applied it to Control first before the technique spread to other titles. Videos show the AI filter reshaping character faces, adding laugh lines and shifting scene lighting.
Performance is the bigger problem. Modders report roughly a 50 percent frame rate loss, with one Blackwell test dropping an RTX 5070 Ti from 71 frames per second to 35 at 4K in Control.
This is an unfinished build being forced into games that were never meant to support it. Nvidia is not expected to ship DLSS 5 officially until the autumn.

consumer-tech.h3: Windows 11 26H2 reaches Release Preview ahead of autumn
consumer-tech.summary: Microsoft pushed Windows 11 version 26H2, build 26300.9278, to the Release Preview Channel on 27 August ahead of general availability later this year.
body: The build gives Insiders and enterprise IT teams first hands on access to this year's annual feature update. It does not install on its own and has to be picked up through the seeker experience in Windows Update.

Most of the changes will already be familiar because Microsoft folded them into monthly updates across the year. Testing suggests 26H2 brings little that is not already available in the August optional update.
The practical effect for most users is a fresh support period without a major operating system upgrade.

consumer-tech.h3: Windows 11 update brings movable taskbar and 35 fixes
consumer-tech.summary: The KB5120998 update for Windows 11 ships 35 changes and fixes, including taskbar repositioning, a resizable Start menu and a new administrator protection feature.
body: Once the staged feature activation lands, users can place the taskbar at the bottom, top, left or right of the screen and choose a smaller layout. The Start menu can be resized and search has been redesigned.
Administrator protection lets users carry out admin tasks with just in time privileges rather than running with elevated rights all the time.
The rollout has not been entirely clean. Reports point to the update breaking cursor styling and resetting wallpapers for some users.

consumer-tech.h3: Edge adds Apple sign-in and scam protection, drops Edge Drop
consumer-tech.summary: The latest Microsoft Edge update lets users sign in with an Apple account and adds automatic scam protection, while retiring Edge Drop and real time video translation.
body: Apple account sign-in widens the options for syncing browser data across devices. The scam protection feature warns users automatically rather than waiting for them to enable it.

The removals are the sting. Edge Drop offered quick file and note transfer between a user's own devices through the browser, and real time video translation was one of the more distinctive Edge features.
The update also brings new admin controls for organisations managing Edge deployments.

consumer-tech.h3: Meta closes another covert recording loophole on its glasses
consumer-tech.summary: Meta is rolling out an update that stops video recording on its smart glasses if the capture LED is covered after recording has already started.
body: The capture light is the main signal to bystanders that a wearer is filming. Covering it with tape or a finger had been a known way to keep recording without the indicator showing.
The change now halts the recording rather than simply warning the wearer, closing a gap that privacy researchers had repeatedly flagged.
Meta has expanded its glasses line steadily, with the Meta Glasses range now on sale in Japan alongside the earlier Ray-Ban Meta and Oakley Meta models.

consumer-tech.h3: Windows 11 starts rolling out Emoji 17.0 support
consumer-tech.summary: Microsoft has begun delivering Emoji 17.0 support to selected Windows 11 users through a Release Preview update, available now in some regions.
body: Emoji updates land unevenly across platforms, so Windows users often wait months after a new set is ratified before the glyphs render properly rather than showing as boxes.
The rollout is limited to select users and regions for now and arrives through the Release Preview channel rather than general availability.
Wider distribution is expected to follow as the update graduates through Microsoft's usual servicing channels.

consumer-tech.h3: Tesla base Model 3 sold out for 2026, deliveries slip to 2027
consumer-tech.summary: Tesla has pushed delivery of the base Model 3 into 2027 after selling out this year's allocation, a rare supply squeeze in a contracting US EV market.
body: The cheapest Model 3 configuration is no longer available with a 2026 delivery date. Buyers ordering now are being quoted next year.
Tesla and every other US EV maker are still working through the fallout of the $7,500 federal tax credit ending in September 2025, which created a boom and bust cycle across the industry.
US EV sales fell sharply after the credit expired, yet Tesla has kept a majority share of the market even as its own volumes dropped.

consumer-tech.h3: Ford tries again on the electric truck America rejected
consumer-tech.summary: Ford says its upcoming affordable electric truck has to be a great vehicle first, with the electric part almost beside the point after a run of failed US electric pickups.
body: Electric trucks have sold far below expectations in the United States. Ford's skunkworks team, led by Alan Clarke, is building the new model around cost and everyday usefulness rather than range headlines and towing records.
The pitch is that buyers were never shopping for an electric truck as a category. They were shopping for a truck, and the previous wave asked them to accept compromises for the powertrain.
The project matters for Ford's wider electric plans, which have been reset since federal incentives lapsed and clean car rules eased.

consumer-tech.h3: Uber puts $100m into charging with robotaxis in mind
consumer-tech.summary: Uber is committing $100m to electric vehicle charging, a bet driven as much by its autonomous vehicle plans as by drivers switching to EVs.
body: Uber's autonomous fleet is mostly electric and will need fast, reliable charging near the areas where those vehicles operate. Charging availability becomes an operating constraint rather than a driver convenience.
The investment lands with EV sales cooled in the United States after the federal tax credit expired, leaving charging network buildout more dependent on commercial fleets than on private buyers.
For drivers on the platform the practical effect is more accessible fast charging, which has been one of the biggest barriers to switching.
